stem: The Group 17 elements are oxidising agents.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain how the Group 17 elements act as oxidising agents.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation to show the reaction in which $\text{Cl}_2$ oxidises aluminium metal.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
A student heats equal amounts of $\text{I}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ in a sealed flask. The student leaves the contents to cool.

State what you would observe during the reaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
$\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{Br}_2$ can each react with $\text{NH}_3$ to give $\text{N}_2$ and a hydrogen halide, HX.

$$3\text{X}_2 + 2\text{NH}_3 \rightarrow \text{N}_2 + 6\text{HX} \text{             X = Cl or Br}$$

The relative bond strengths of X-X and H-X determine the difference in enthalpy change of the two reactions.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Describe and explain the difference in the X-X bond strengths of $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{Br}_2$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Describe the relative thermal stabilities of $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HBr}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Define enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}$.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
Table 1.1 gives data relevant to the reaction of $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ with $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$.

Table 1.1

| compound | enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}$/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$ | $-46$ |
| $\text{HCl}\text{(g)}$ | $-92$ |

Use the data in Table 1.1 to calculate the enthalpy change of the reaction of $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ with $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
$\text{I}_2$ reacts with $\text{NH}_3$ to form $\text{NI}_3$.

Predict the shape of a molecule of $\text{NI}_3$. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Table 1.2 shows some information about reactions of $\text{NaCl}$, $\text{NaBr}$ and $\text{NaI}$.

Table 1.2

|  | $\text{NaCl}$ | $\text{NaBr}$ | $\text{NaI}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| observation with $\text{Ag}^{+}\text{(aq)}$ | white precipitate |  |  |
| type of reaction with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ | acid-base | acid-base, then redox | acid-base, then redox |
| observations with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ |  |  |  |
| • black solid • yellow solid • effervescence |  |  |  |

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest an identity for the species that produces each observation in the reaction of $\text{NaI}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Table 1.3 gives some information about $\text{MgCl}_2$ and $\text{SiCl}_4$.

Table 1.3

|  | $\text{MgCl}_2$ | $\text{SiCl}_4$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| electrical conductivity when liquid | conducts | does not conduct |
| observation when added to water | dissolves | vigorous reaction |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Explain the difference between the electrical conductivity of liquid $\text{MgCl}_2$ and of liquid $\text{SiCl}_4$. Refer to bonding and relevant particles in your answer.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest the pH of the solutions that form when each chloride is added to water.
